ARBA00026480 negative regulation of macromolecule metabolic process (GO:0010605)

View original ARBA rule on UniProt

Type: ARBA
Status: COMPLETE
Action: SPLIT
Confidence: 0.80
Rule as retrieved: 2026-11-09
Condition sets examined: 343 of 343

Description

Assigns GO:0010605 negative regulation of macromolecule metabolic process through 343 alternative condition sets built from InterPro entries, PANTHER families and CATH FunFams; 107 sets carry a taxon condition. GO:0010605 is a high-level grouping term whose descendants include negative regulation of gene expression, mRNA catabolism and RNA-mediated gene silencing.

The domain overlap table is not shown for this review. It is drawn from a cached analysis of the rule's condition sets, and the cache does not match the sets recorded here.

Review Summary

Accuracy: all 343 live condition sets were queried against Swiss-Prot on 2026-11-09, counting a match as supported when it carries GO:0010605 (negative regulation of macromolecule metabolic process) or an is_a/part_of descendant with evidence other than ARBA. Every set has reviewed matches; in 249 sets every reviewed match is supported, in 94 some are not, and no set is wholly unsupported (2649 reviewed matches: 2116 supported, 403 carrying the term only from ARBA, 130 not carrying it). The partly supported sets were not adjudicated one by one. Meaning and parsimony: the term is true of most matches and says almost nothing. GO:0010605 has 524 descendants and is in the GO subset gocheck_do_not_annotate, that is, a grouping term not meant for direct annotation. The sets resolve into unrelated families that each carry a far more specific curated term: Dicer (miRNA processing), HP1 chromobox proteins (heterochromatin formation), Hes/Hey and LexA repressors (negative regulation of transcription), DCP2 (mRNA decapping), ZFP36L1/2 (3'-UTR-mediated mRNA destabilization), APOBEC3 (restriction of retroviral replication) and others. For a few units the term holds only through a phenotype annotation, for example the FGF receptors of set 60. rule_redundancy.tsv finds 313 of the rule's 343 sets already matched by a rule asserting a more specific term, and QuickGO holds no annotation attributed to this rule (2026-11-12), so as served the rule produces nothing.

Action Rationale

The rule is not wrong so much as empty: its consequent is a do-not-annotate grouping term, nine tenths of its sets are covered by rules with more specific terms, and it emits no annotation. The useful content is in the condition sets, which identify real families. Sets already covered should be dropped and the remainder re-homed, family by family, under the specific term that curated annotation supports. Units were assigned for 26 sets chosen because their signatures name a family; confidence reflects that sample. Retiring the rule outright would also be defensible, since it emits nothing.

Biological Meaning

TRUE BUT UNINFORMATIVE

Eleven of the thirteen units examined carry a curated descendant of the consequent that names their actual role; the consequent is their only common ancestor. One unit (FGF receptors) fits only by phenotype annotation, and one (CodY, sets 34 and 58) has no curated term under the consequent on its best-studied member. The sample is the 26 recorded sets whose signature labels name a family unambiguously; one member per unit was looked up in QuickGO.

The consequent term has 524 descendant terms. 313 condition set(s) are also matched by a rule asserting a more specific term. 26 condition set(s) were examined for this judgement.

Assessments

REDUNDANT

rule_redundancy.tsv: 313 of 343 condition sets are matched by a rule asserting a more specific term, and such sets emit nothing because UniProt keeps the most specific ARBA term. QuickGO lists 0 annotations with ARBA:ARBA00026480 as source (2026-11-12) and UniProt reports 0 proteins for the rule. Several families are also entered more than once through different signatures, for example LexA in Gammaproteobacteria by sets 5 and 38, each with 157 reviewed matches. rules/arba/_interpro2go.txt has no InterPro entry mapped to GO:0010605.

TOO_BROAD

GO:0010605 has 524 is_a/part_of descendants (rule_redundancy.tsv) and is in the GO subset gocheck_do_not_annotate (OLS, 2026-11-12). QuickGO holds no direct annotation to it from any source. Every unit examined that fits the term has a more specific curated descendant.

TOO_NARROW

107 of 343 sets carry a taxon condition. Several restrict a widely distributed family to the organism where its curated annotations are: Hes/Hey to Mus (set 4), APOBEC3 to Homo (sets 17, 54), sirtuins to Saccharomyces (set 24), FGF receptors to Mus (set 60). That is narrow coverage following the training annotations, not wrong annotation. Others follow the biology, such as LexA restricted to bacterial classes.

Corrections (6)

Claims made by an earlier version of this review that were withdrawn, with the evidence that refuted them.

Withdrawn claimCorrection
The rule includes kinases (IPR000571), metabolic enzymes such as ribonucleoside-diphosphate reductase (IPR000999), glycosyl transferases (IPR000953) and biosynthetic enzymes (IPR001313).
wrong identifier meaning · 2026-11-10		 None of these entries is what it was called. They are RNA- and chromatin-binding signatures of proteins that repress gene expression.
  • InterPro IPR000571: Zinc finger, CCCH-type
  • InterPro IPR000999: Ribonuclease III domain
  • InterPro IPR000953: Chromo/chromo shadow domain
  • InterPro IPR001313: Pumilio RNA-binding repeat
  • InterPro IPR001650: Helicase, C-terminal domain-like
The protein families in the rule have no shared basis for negative regulation; each domain was assessed on its own.
conjunction ignored · 2026-11-10		 The domains occur only in conjunctions, and the conjunctions identify specific families of negative regulators.
  • Live CS2 = IPR000999 AND IPR001650 AND IPR027417 (Dicer): 48 Swiss-Prot matches, 47 supported
  • Live CS3 = IPR000953 AND IPR023779 AND IPR051219 (HP1 family): 15 matches, 14 supported
  • Live CS21 = IPR000571 AND IPR007635 AND Euarchontoglires (ZFP36L1/2): 5 matches, 5 supported
  • Live CS4 = IPR003650 AND IPR011598 AND Mus (Hes/Hey): 12 matches, 12 supported
Proteins that catalyse macromolecule metabolism do the opposite of negative regulation, so literature contradicts the rule.
ontology misread · 2026-11-10		 Catalysing a macromolecular reaction is not positive regulation. In GO, mRNA catabolism and RNA-mediated silencing are themselves kinds of negative regulation of gene expression, which is under GO:0010605. No publication was cited for the contradiction.
  • QuickGO is_a ancestors of GO:0000956 nuclear-transcribed mRNA catabolic process include GO:0010605
  • QuickGO is_a ancestors of GO:0031047 regulatory ncRNA-mediated gene silencing include GO:0010605
  • QuickGO is_a ancestors of GO:0010629 negative regulation of gene expression include GO:0010605
GO:0010605 is a specific regulatory function that requires evidence of inhibitory activity.
general is not wrong · 2026-11-10		 It is a broad grouping term with 489 is_a descendants.
  • QuickGO GO:0010605 descendants (is_a): 489 terms (2026-11-09)
343 condition sets exceed an analysis threshold of 12 and show over-engineering; 70% of sets lack a taxon restriction, so the rule would generate thousands of false positives and should be deprecated.
size as evidence · 2026-11-10		 Neither the number of sets nor the absence of a taxon condition is evidence about any annotation. The condition sets had not been recorded when this was written. Queried set by set, no set is unsupported.
  • Live rule: 343 sets, 107 with a taxon condition
  • Swiss-Prot support: 249 sets fully supported, 94 partly, 0 unsupported
No verdict can be given because 94 partly supported sets were not adjudicated match by match.
meaning not judged · 2026-11-12		 The rule-level verdict does not depend on those matches. The consequent is a do-not-annotate grouping term with 524 descendants, the families selected each carry a more specific curated term, 320 of 355 sets are covered by rules with more specific terms, and the rule emits no annotation. The rule should be split by family under specific terms.
  • projects/ARBA_REVIEW/rule_redundancy.tsv: ARBA00026480 go_descendants 524, condition_sets 343, covered_sets 313
  • OLS GO:0010605 in_subset: gocheck_do_not_annotate (2026-11-12)
  • QuickGO annotation search withFrom=ARBA:ARBA00026480: 0 hits (2026-11-12)
  • Q9UPY3 GO:0035196 IDA PMID:15973356; P45973 GO:0031507 IDA PMID:19783980; Q07352 GO:0061158 IDA PMID:15467755

  go_annotations:
  - go_id: GO:0010605
    go_label: negative regulation of macromolecule metabolic process
    aspect: BP
  entries: []
  reviewed_protein_count: 0
  unreviewed_protein_count: 0
  created_date: '2021-10-20'
  modified_date: '2026-07-18'
  retrieved_date: '2026-11-09'
  source_condition_set_count: 343
review_summary: >-
  Accuracy: all 343 live condition sets were queried against Swiss-Prot on 2026-11-09, counting a match
  as supported when it carries GO:0010605 (negative regulation of macromolecule metabolic process) or
  an is_a/part_of descendant with evidence other than ARBA. Every set has reviewed matches; in 249 sets
  every reviewed match is supported, in 94 some are not, and no set is wholly unsupported (2649 reviewed
  matches: 2116 supported, 403 carrying the term only from ARBA, 130 not carrying it). The partly supported
  sets were not adjudicated one by one. Meaning and parsimony: the term is true of most matches and says
  almost nothing. GO:0010605 has 524 descendants and is in the GO subset gocheck_do_not_annotate, that
  is, a grouping term not meant for direct annotation. The sets resolve into unrelated families that each
  carry a far more specific curated term: Dicer (miRNA processing), HP1 chromobox proteins (heterochromatin
  formation), Hes/Hey and LexA repressors (negative regulation of transcription), DCP2 (mRNA decapping),
  ZFP36L1/2 (3'-UTR-mediated mRNA destabilization), APOBEC3 (restriction of retroviral replication) and
  others. For a few units the term holds only through a phenotype annotation, for example the FGF receptors
  of set 60. rule_redundancy.tsv finds 313 of the rule's 343 sets already matched by a rule asserting
  a more specific term, and QuickGO holds no annotation attributed to this rule (2026-11-12), so as served
  the rule produces nothing.
action: SPLIT
action_rationale: >-
  The rule is not wrong so much as empty: its consequent is a do-not-annotate grouping term, nine tenths
  of its sets are covered by rules with more specific terms, and it emits no annotation. The useful content
  is in the condition sets, which identify real families. Sets already covered should be dropped and the
  remainder re-homed, family by family, under the specific term that curated annotation supports. Units
  were assigned for 26 sets chosen because their signatures name a family; confidence reflects that sample.
  Retiring the rule outright would also be defensible, since it emits nothing.
confidence: 0.8
suggested_modifications:
- >-
  Stop asserting GO:0010605 (negative regulation of macromolecule metabolic process); it is in gocheck_do_not_annotate.
- >-
  Drop the condition sets already matched by rules asserting a more specific term (313 of 343 in rule_redundancy.tsv;
  covering terms include GO:0010629 negative regulation of gene expression, GO:0010558 negative regulation
  of macromolecule biosynthetic process, GO:0051253 negative regulation of RNA metabolic process, GO:0051053
  negative regulation of DNA metabolic process and GO:0031400 negative regulation of protein modification
  process).
- >-
  Move the remaining sets to rules for the specific term of their family, as listed in biological_units:
  sets 2, 45, 46, 49 to GO:0035196 (miRNA processing); sets 3, 6, 39 to GO:0031507 (heterochromatin formation);
  sets 4, 12, 44 to GO:0000122 (negative regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II); sets 1, 5,
  26, 38 to GO:0045892 (negative regulation of DNA-templated transcription); sets 14, 57 to GO:0000290
  (deadenylation-dependent decapping of nuclear-transcribed mRNA); set 21 to GO:0061158 (3'-UTR-mediated
  mRNA destabilization); set 15 to GO:0017148 (negative regulation of translation); set 16 to GO:2000632

corrections:
- date: '2026-11-10'
  withdrawn_claim: The rule includes kinases (IPR000571), metabolic enzymes such as
    ribonucleoside-diphosphate reductase (IPR000999), glycosyl transferases (IPR000953) and
    biosynthetic enzymes (IPR001313).
  correction: None of these entries is what it was called. They are RNA- and chromatin-binding
    signatures of proteins that repress gene expression.
  error_type: WRONG_IDENTIFIER_MEANING
  evidence:
  - 'InterPro IPR000571: Zinc finger, CCCH-type'
  - 'InterPro IPR000999: Ribonuclease III domain'
  - 'InterPro IPR000953: Chromo/chromo shadow domain'
  - 'InterPro IPR001313: Pumilio RNA-binding repeat'
  - 'InterPro IPR001650: Helicase, C-terminal domain-like'
- date: '2026-11-10'
  withdrawn_claim: The protein families in the rule have no shared basis for negative regulation;
    each domain was assessed on its own.
  correction: The domains occur only in conjunctions, and the conjunctions identify specific
    families of negative regulators.
  error_type: CONJUNCTION_IGNORED
  evidence:
  - 'Live CS2 = IPR000999 AND IPR001650 AND IPR027417 (Dicer): 48 Swiss-Prot matches, 47 supported'
  - 'Live CS3 = IPR000953 AND IPR023779 AND IPR051219 (HP1 family): 15 matches, 14 supported'
  - 'Live CS21 = IPR000571 AND IPR007635 AND Euarchontoglires (ZFP36L1/2): 5 matches, 5 supported'
  - 'Live CS4 = IPR003650 AND IPR011598 AND Mus (Hes/Hey): 12 matches, 12 supported'
- date: '2026-11-10'
  withdrawn_claim: Proteins that catalyse macromolecule metabolism do the opposite of negative
    regulation, so literature contradicts the rule.
  correction: Catalysing a macromolecular reaction is not positive regulation. In GO, mRNA
    catabolism and RNA-mediated silencing are themselves kinds of negative regulation of gene
    expression, which is under GO:0010605. No publication was cited for the contradiction.
  error_type: ONTOLOGY_MISREAD
  evidence:
  - QuickGO is_a ancestors of GO:0000956 nuclear-transcribed mRNA catabolic process include
    GO:0010605
  - QuickGO is_a ancestors of GO:0031047 regulatory ncRNA-mediated gene silencing include GO:0010605
  - QuickGO is_a ancestors of GO:0010629 negative regulation of gene expression include GO:0010605
- date: '2026-11-10'
  withdrawn_claim: GO:0010605 is a specific regulatory function that requires evidence of inhibitory
    activity.
  correction: It is a broad grouping term with 489 is_a descendants.
  error_type: GENERAL_IS_NOT_WRONG
  evidence:
  - 'QuickGO GO:0010605 descendants (is_a): 489 terms (2026-11-09)'
- date: '2026-11-10'
  withdrawn_claim: 343 condition sets exceed an analysis threshold of 12 and show over-engineering;
    70% of sets lack a taxon restriction, so the rule would generate thousands of false positives
    and should be deprecated.
  correction: Neither the number of sets nor the absence of a taxon condition is evidence about any
    annotation. The condition sets had not been recorded when this was written. Queried set by set,
    no set is unsupported.
  error_type: SIZE_AS_EVIDENCE
  evidence:
  - 'Live rule: 343 sets, 107 with a taxon condition'
  - 'Swiss-Prot support: 249 sets fully supported, 94 partly, 0 unsupported'
- date: '2026-11-12'
  withdrawn_claim: >-
    No verdict can be given because 94 partly supported sets were not adjudicated match by match.
  correction: >-
    The rule-level verdict does not depend on those matches. The consequent is a do-not-annotate grouping
    term with 524 descendants, the families selected each carry a more specific curated term, 320 of 355
    sets are covered by rules with more specific terms, and the rule emits no annotation. The rule should
    be split by family under specific terms.
  error_type: MEANING_NOT_JUDGED

  - 'QuickGO annotation search withFrom=ARBA:ARBA00026480: 0 hits (2026-11-12)'

    Q9UPY3 GO:0035196 IDA PMID:15973356; P45973 GO:0031507 IDA PMID:19783980; Q07352 GO:0061158 IDA PMID:15467755
parsimony:
  assessment: REDUNDANT
  notes: >-
    rule_redundancy.tsv: 313 of 343 condition sets are matched by a rule asserting a more specific term,
    and such sets emit nothing because UniProt keeps the most specific ARBA term. QuickGO lists 0 annotations
    with ARBA:ARBA00026480 as source (2026-11-12) and UniProt reports 0 proteins for the rule. Several
    families are also entered more than once through different signatures, for example LexA in Gammaproteobacteria
    by sets 5 and 38, each with 157 reviewed matches. rules/arba/_interpro2go.txt has no InterPro entry
    mapped to GO:0010605.
go_specificity:
  assessment: TOO_BROAD
  notes: >-
    GO:0010605 has 524 is_a/part_of descendants (rule_redundancy.tsv) and is in the GO subset gocheck_do_not_annotate
    (OLS, 2026-11-12). QuickGO holds no direct annotation to it from any source. Every unit examined that
    fits the term has a more specific curated descendant.
taxonomic_scope:
  assessment: TOO_NARROW
  notes: >-
    107 of 343 sets carry a taxon condition. Several restrict a widely distributed family to the organism
    where its curated annotations are: Hes/Hey to Mus (set 4), APOBEC3 to Homo (sets 17, 54), sirtuins
    to Saccharomyces (set 24), FGF receptors to Mus (set 60). That is narrow coverage following the training
    annotations, not wrong annotation. Others follow the biology, such as LexA restricted to bacterial
    classes.
